answer: Each identity must first post a bonded deposit into the validator's kernel, a 5000-token escrow that unlocks voting weight. When an agent submits grades, verifiers compare them against the consensus canyon separating honest scores from outliers; a divergence beyond two standard deviations flags the identity. The deposit is then slashed on-ledger, leaving a permanent slash trail that any peer can audit, driving that key's reputation to its nadir. Faking 10000 identities now demands $50000 in forfeitable stake, so sockpuppet farming multiplies capital at risk rather than inflating influence.
